correctness.rationale: Every code vertex lies in exactly four closed neighborhoods; among 24 distinct nonempty closed-neighborhood signatures at most k are singleton, so 4k>=k+2(24-k), i.e. k>=10. Independent C++ direct signature enumeration of all C(24,10)=1,961,256 and C(24,11)=2,496,144 candidates gives zero size-ten codes and exactly 384 size-eleven codes; monotonicity eliminates sizes below 10. Independent NetworkX construction from the LCF sequence and exact isomorphism enumeration gives 32 graph automorphisms, all checked as bijections preserving incidences; orbit partition of all 384 codes gives 13 disjoint orbits of sizes 16 twice and 32 eleven times and reproduces all 13 listed representatives. This exhausts the only finite candidate layers needed for minimum, rather than sampling.
residual_risks: Only ordinary single-vertex closed-neighborhood identification, not stronger (1,<=ell)-codes or other cages.

value.rationale: The McGee graph is the canonical extremal cubic (3,7)-cage; identifying codes are a natural sensor/location-discrimination invariant. The exact minimum, full 384 optimum multiplicity and 13 symmetry classes provide an independently usable complete classification of optimal configurations and distinguish multiple geometry types.
residual_risks: Finite invariant of one graph; not a uniform theorem for arbitrary cages.

final_claim: On the McGee 24-vertex cubic girth-seven cage with LCF [12,7,-7]^8, the minimum ordinary radius-one identifying-code size is 11; exactly 384 optimum codes exist, split into 13 orbits under full Aut(H) of order 32 (two 16-element and eleven 32-element orbits), with the 13 supplied representatives.
